rentTypical1brUsd.sourceId: Statistics Canada / Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation · Average rents by bedroom type, Rental Market Survey (table 34-10-0133-01), October 2025
rentTypical1brUsd.method: Typical one-bedroom rent = average rent of one-bedroom units in purpose-built apartment structures of three units and over, by census metropolitan area; existing tenancies, so below asking rents. The table has no national row, so the cost adjustment compares each city's two-bedroom average with CMHC's national two-bedroom average (Canada 10,000+, C$1,550, Rental Market Report 2025, Table 1.0). Where a city has no city-level cost, its national estimate is scaled by its rent: national × (1 + s × (rent ÷ national rent − 1)), with s, the weight of rent in the price level, fitted in each build on US cities against BEA price parities. Whistler and Banff are not surveyed; Whitehorse is suppressed. Input: scripts/build-dataset/inputs/rents-ca.csv.

rentTypical1brUsd.sourceId: ANIL / Ministère de la Transition écologique · Carte des loyers 2025: advertised rent per m² for 1–2 room flats, by commune
rentTypical1brUsd.method: Typical one-bedroom rent = the modelled advertised rent per m² (charges included, unfurnished, Q3 2025) × 37 m², the reference flat. Paris, Lyon and Marseille are their arrondissements weighted by number of ads. National reference: all communes weighted by number of ads, which leans towards large rental markets. Where a city has no city-level cost, its national estimate is scaled by its rent: national × (1 + s × (rent ÷ national rent − 1)), with s, the weight of rent in the price level, fitted in each build on US cities against BEA price parities. Input: scripts/build-dataset/inputs/rents-fr.csv.
